record.paper_title: On open problems based on fuzzy filters of pseudo BCK-algebras
record.context_brief: Equivalence of implicative and Boolean pseudo-filters
record.original_question: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations customarily written as ⇀ and ⇝, order relation inherited from those operations, and top element 1. In the bounded case, assume A also has a least element 0 in the sense used for bounded pseudo-BCK algebras. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and closed under the pseudo-BCK filter rule: if x is in F and either x ⇀ y or x ⇝ y is in F, then y is in F. Such a pseudo-filter F is called implicative when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F. It is called Boolean when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F. In pseudo-BCK algebras, and separately in bounded pseudo-BCK algebras, are the notions of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter equivalent?

evidence.quote: Is the notion of implicative pseudo-filter equivalent to the notion of Boolean filter?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(A;\rightharpoonup,\rightsquigarrow,1)$ be a pseudo-BCK algebra, where $\rightharpoonup$ and $\rightsquigarrow$ are binary operations on $A$, $1\in A$ is the top element, and the partial order $\le$ is defined by $x\le y \iff x\rightharpoonup y = 1 \iff x\rightsquigarrow y = 1$. A nonempty subset $F\subseteq A$ is called a pseudo-filter if (i) $F$ is upward closed (whenever $x\in F$ and $x\le y$ then $y\in F$), and (ii) for all $x,y\in A$, if $x\in F$ and either $x\rightharpoonup y\in F$ or $x\rightsquigarrow y\in F$, then $y\in F$.

A pseudo-filter $F$ is called an implicative pseudo-filter if for all $x,y\in A$:
- $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightharpoonup x \in F \implies x\in F$, and
- $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightsquigarrow x \in F \implies x\in F$.

A pseudo-filter $F$ is called a Boolean filter if for all $x,y\in A$:
- $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x \in F \implies x\in F$, and
- $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x \in F \implies x\in F$.

Question: In an arbitrary pseudo-BCK algebra (and separately in a bounded pseudo-BCK algebra, where $A$ additionally has a least element $0$), are the notions of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter equivalent?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work titled "Further Complete Solutions to Four Open Problems on Filter of Logical Algebras" (International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems / Atlantis Press, 2019) addresses this question and establishes that in pseudo-BCK algebras the notion of implicative pseudo-filter coincides with the notion of Boolean filter, providing a complete solution to the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Further Complete Solutions to Four Open Problems on Filter of Logical Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Provides complete solutions to open problems on filters of logical algebras, including the equivalence of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter in pseudo-BCK algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter in pseudo-BCK algebras has been established.

status_evidence.title: Further Complete Solutions to Four Open Problems on Filter (PDF)
status_evidence.snippet: By characterizing Boolean filter and implicative filter in pseudo BCK-algebra, the essential equivalent relation between these two filters is revealed.
status_evidence.claim: Implicative pseudo-filter is Boolean filter in pseudo-BCK algebras.
